newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch 1997 state debt lower than forecast - paper.
newsitem.headline: Dutch 1997 state debt lower than forecast - paper.

text.p: Dutch public sector debt is falling faster than previously forecast according to government figures, Dutch newspaper Het Financieele Dagblad reported on Friday.

The newspaper, quoting unpublished figures from the government's Central Planning Bureau (CPB), said public debt as a proportion of gross domestic product (GDP) would drop to 74.6 percent in 1997 from 78.8 percent in 1996.
The government's last officially published forecast for public debt in 1997 was 76.2 percent.
A CPB spokesman declined to comment on the report saying the bureau was set to publish new forecasts on April 3.

The Maastricht Treaty convergence criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU) stipulate that a country's public debt should be no more than 60 percent of GDP or should be declining at a satisfactory pace towards that level.
